issues.t: Coolant leaks and overheating
issues.sym: The low-coolant warning comes on, the temperature gauge climbs, you smell something sweet, or you keep having to top up the coolant. Some owners have it come back after a repair.
issues.why: Coolant loss is the most common owner complaint on the first F-Pace, mostly on gas models and especially 2017. Leaking pumps, hoses and plastic cooling parts are typical causes, and some owners report engine damage after running low.
issues.next: Stop and let the engine cool if the gauge rises or a coolant warning appears. Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak before more driving, since overheating can ruin the engine.

issues.t: Leaking fuel injector flooding a cylinder
issues.sym: Rough running, a misfire or check engine light, hard starting, or in the worst case an engine that will not turn over.
issues.why: Owners report fuel injectors failing on the F-Pace. A leaking injector can fill a cylinder with fuel while the car sits, and the trapped liquid can lock the engine (hydrolock) and bend internal parts.
issues.next: If the engine misfires or smells of raw fuel, have the injectors checked soon. If it will not crank after a misfire, do not keep trying to start it; have it towed so the cylinder can be inspected.

issues.t: Timing chain and balance shaft wear (2.0L diesel)
issues.sym: A metallic rattle on cold start, a check engine light with camshaft timing codes, oil pressure warnings, or the engine cutting out.
issues.why: The 2.0L Ingenium diesel is known for timing chains that stretch, weak tensioners and worn balance shaft bearings. Metal from the wear spreads through the oil, and short trips that thin the oil speed it up.
issues.next: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle. Have the timing chain checked right away, and change the oil more often than the long factory interval. Caught early, a timing repair can save the engine.

issues.t: Diesel particulate filter clogging and oil dilution
issues.sym: A diesel particulate filter (DPF) warning, reduced power, or an oil level that rises on the dipstick.
issues.why: The DPF burns off soot during longer drives. Lots of short trips stop it from finishing, so soot builds up and extra diesel ends up in the engine oil, thinning it and wearing the engine faster.
issues.next: Take the car on a steady highway drive of 20 minutes or more when the DPF light shows. If it stays on, have the filter checked, and change the oil more often if most of your driving is short trips.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch (2.0L turbo gas)
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine, especially on a cold start, a check engine light, or rough running.
issues.why: The gas 2.0L Ingenium four-cylinder has a record of stretched timing chains and faulty variable valve timing solenoids. Long oil-change intervals are thought to make it worse.
issues.next: Have any new rattle checked by a shop quickly. Changing the oil sooner than the factory schedule (around every 10,000 miles) is simple protection.

issues.t: High oil consumption (2.0L turbo gas)
issues.sym: You need to add oil between services, or a low oil level warning appears.
issues.why: The gas 2.0L Ingenium engine is reported to use more oil than it should on some cars.
issues.next: Check the oil level every few fill-ups and top up with the correct oil. If it is using a lot, ask a dealer to run an oil consumption test while any warranty still applies.

issues.t: Touchscreen infotainment or navigation failure
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, goes black, reboots, or the navigation stops working.
issues.why: Owners report failures of the infotainment system and GPS on the first F-Pace. Some need software updates; others need the control unit replaced.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the latest software update first. If the screen stays dead, the unit may need replacing; ask whether the warranty covers it.

issues.t: 12-volt battery draining and no-start
issues.sym: A low battery warning, the doors will not unlock, or the car will not start after sitting a few days or after short trips.
issues.why: Jaguar has issued service bulletins for 12-volt battery problems. On 2021 models, software in the door modules can keep the car from going fully to sleep and slowly drain the battery.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and ask a dealer about the door module software update. If the car sits often, a battery maintainer helps.

issues.t: Coolant hose rubbing on drive belt (3.0L V6)
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the car or the coolant level drops.
issues.why: On some early 2017 V6 models, a clip that holds a coolant hose from the thermostat housing was left off, so the hose can rub against the engine drive belt and wear through.
issues.next: Ask a Jaguar dealer to check the hose and clip. It is a quick inspection, and fixing it early prevents a coolant leak.

issues.t: Cracked oil filter housing fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: An oil smell, visible oil around the engine, smoke from the engine bay, or a low oil warning.
issues.why: The oil filter housing can crack and spray oil into the engine bay, where it can catch fire on hot parts. Recall 24V-451.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check for open recalls with your VIN and book the free repair.

issues.t: Loss of drive power from DC-DC converter fault (recall)
issues.sym: Electrical warning messages, then the car may lose drive power or fail to restart, and exterior lights may go out.
issues.why: On mild-hybrid models, the DC-DC converter that charges the 12-volt system can overload during high electrical demand or fail from a software error. Recalls 26V-248 and 26V-599; the final fix is still being prepared.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for these recalls and get the interim software update. If warnings appear, pull over somewhere safe.

issues.t: Blocked cam carrier oil passage causing oil leak (recall)
issues.sym: An oil leak or a burning oil smell from under the hood.
issues.why: An oil passage in the engine's cam carrier may be blocked, which can force oil out and create a fire risk. Recall 23V-045.
issues.next: Have a dealer run your VIN and do the free inspection and repair.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not display (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview or 3D surround camera picture does not appear when reversing.
issues.why: The module that runs the cameras can overheat and shut the image off. Recall 24V-677.
issues.next: Get the free module replacement. Until then, check mirrors and look behind you when reversing.

issues.t: Front seat belt pretensioners may be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; the belts may not hold you properly in a crash.
issues.why: The front seat belt pretensioners may have been damaged during production. Recall 22V-524.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect and replace the belts free of charge.

issues.t: Missing audio module silences safety chimes (recall)
issues.sym: No seat belt reminder chime, turn signal sound or driver-assist warnings.
issues.why: Some cars were built without the audio amplifier module that produces these alert sounds. Recall 22V-580.
issues.next: Have the dealer install the missing module free of charge.

issues.t: Rear turn signals may not light correctly (recall)
issues.sym: A rear turn signal looks dim, does not flash, or does not light at all.
issues.why: The wrong tail lights may have been fitted at the factory. Recall 22V-525.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the lights and replace them free if needed.

issues.t: Child seat belt locking may release early (recall)
issues.sym: A belt pulled all the way out to install a child seat does not stay locked.
issues.why: The automatic locking retractor in the seat belt can switch off before it should, so a child seat may not be held tight. Recall 21V-667.
issues.next: Have the belts inspected and replaced free of charge. Check that any child seat is tight until then.

issues.t: Automatic high beam indicator missing (recall)
issues.sym: The dashboard does not show that the high beams are on when the automatic high beam turns them on.
issues.why: A software error means the high-beam indicator does not light in automatic mode, which breaks federal lighting rules. Recall 21V-118.
issues.next: Get the free software update at a dealer.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley bolt may break (recall)
issues.sym: Noise from the front of the engine, a belt or charging warning, or sudden engine failure.
issues.why: The bolt that holds the crankshaft pulley may have been made incorrectly and can snap. Recall 19V-039.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the bolt replaced free of charge.

issues.t: Fuel rail end caps may leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell around the car or in the cabin.
issues.why: End caps on the fuel rail of the 2.0L gas engine can leak fuel into the engine bay, a fire risk. Recall 18V-090.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell fuel and have the dealer replace the fuel rail free of charge.

issues.t: Instrument cluster may go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The instrument screen goes blank while driving, hiding speed and warning lights.
issues.why: A software fault can make the digital cluster go dark for a time. Recalls 17V-678 and 18V-052.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Get the free software update. If it happens, slow down and pull over safely.

issues.t: Rear driveshaft may separate (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or bang from under the car, then loss of drive.
issues.why: A small number of early cars got a rear driveshaft that was too short and could come apart. Recall 17V-153.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers inspect and replace incorrect driveshafts free of charge.
